newsitem.title: CHINA: China Q1 state fixed asset investment up 17.2 pct.
newsitem.headline: China Q1 state fixed asset investment up 17.2 pct.

text.p: Investment in fixed assets by China's state-owned firms is expected to total 152.15 billion yuan ($18.33 billion) in the first three months of 1997, up 17.2 percent year-on-year, the China Business Daily said on Monday.
Most investment would go toward renovating factories and into real estate, the newspaper said.
"China will make the real estate industry into a new growth point for the national economy," the newspaper said without elaborating.
Infrastructure investment would be strictly controlled to avoid the unnecessary duplication of projects, it said.
Authorities would put forth proposals to restructure sectors in crisis, such as the textile and machinery industries, it said but gave no further details.
State media have forecast China's fixed asset investment will grow by 17.6 percent in 1997 to 2.775 billion yuan.
